evidence.quote: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chips to reduce its reliance on products from Nvidia and Huawei
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek is developing its own AI inference chips, per three unnamed sources cited by Reuters; the project is at an early stage and DeepSeek did not confirm it.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (citing three unnamed sources)
evidence.original_who: three sources familiar with the plans

evidence.quote: Nvidia's position in China is effectively at zero and will remain that way.
evidence.one_line: Analyst Richard Windsor of Radio Free Mobile says Nvidia's China position is effectively zero and will stay that way.
evidence.speaker: Richard Windsor, Radio Free Mobile

evidence.quote: Huawei has expanded its domestic market share and now controls around half of China's AI chip market, which is valued at approximately US$50 billion.
evidence.one_line: Huawei is said to control around half of China's AI chip market, valued at about US$50 billion.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (via idnfinancials.com)

evidence.quote: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, called Jalapeno, last month in collaboration with Broadcom
evidence.one_line: OpenAI introduced its first inference chip, Jalapeno, in June 2026 in collaboration with Broadcom.
evidence.speaker: Reuters (via idnfinancials.com)

evidence.quote: Reuters previously reported that the company was preparing its first funding round worth US$7 billion, with a valuation of between US$52 billion and US$59 billion
evidence.one_line: DeepSeek was reported to be preparing a first funding round of US$7 billion at a valuation of US$52 billion to US$59 billion.
